answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring every voting identity to claim a unique scarce slot in a public capability atlas, such as a distinct hardware root or address block. Only one live key may occupy a slot. Fresh claims carry only a thin plume of influence until the lock ages and independent operators countersign it; only then does the identity reach a voting summit. Software clones cannot mint extra slots, so an attacker who wants majority weight must buy and operate as many independent slots as honest agents, paying capital and upkeep that grow linearly with each extra persona.
